summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly integrated AI and ML capabilities directly into their core engines, eliminating the need to move data to external systems for inference and model training. By 2026, vector search has become a foundational capability across virtually all major data platforms, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities according to ACI Infotech. The competitive landscape is shifting from purpose-built vector databases toward general-purpose platforms with embedded AI, as Snowflake, Google, Amazon, Databricks, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL extensions all offer native LLM integration, embedding generation, and semantic search within their existing infrastructure.

databases.name: Snowflake
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of fully managed ML and LLM functions directly within the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. It includes Cortex LLM Functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, TRANSLATE, EXTRACT_ANSWER) that run inference on leading models including Mistral, LLaMA, and Snowflake Arctic without data leaving the platform. Cortex Search enables hybrid vector and keyword search over enterprise data, while Cortex Analyst allows natural language querying of structured data. Snowflake Postgres (generally available in 2026) now runs natively in the AI Data Cloud with pgvector support, and the Unistore capability eliminates the transactional-analytical divide for real-time AI applications. Cortex Fine-tuning allows organizations to fine-tune open-source LLMs on their proprietary Snowflake data.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Mistral, LLaMA 3, Snowflake Arctic, Reka, and Jamba models via Cortex LLM Functions. Supports bring-your-own-model via external functions and integrates with Hugging Face. Cortex Analyst connects LLMs directly to structured Snowflake tables for natural language querying.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits. LLM inference costs vary by model and token count, typically ranging from 0.013 to 0.20 credits per 1,000 tokens depending on model size. Cortex Search is priced on indexed data volume and query volume. Snowflake Postgres pricing follows standard Snowflake compute and storage credit consumption. Overall costs are bundled into existing Snowflake contracts for many enterprise customers.

databases.name: Google BigQuery
databases.description: BigQuery ML enables data analysts and data scientists to create and execute machine learning models directly within BigQuery using standard SQL statements, removing the need to export data. Supported model types include linear regression, binary and multiclass logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, time series forecasting (ARIMA+), XGBoost, deep neural networks, AutoML Tables, and imported TensorFlow or PyTorch models. BigQuery's deep integration with Vertex AI allows calling hosted LLMs including Gemini models directly from SQL using ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions. BigQuery Vector Search provides approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns stored natively in BigQuery tables, enabling semantic search and RAG pipelines without a separate vector store.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration with Google Gemini (1.0 Pro, 1.5 Pro, 1.5 Flash) and PaLM 2 models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT SQL function. Supports text embedding generation via ML.EMBED_TEXT using Gecko embedding models. Remote model connections allow calling any Vertex AI endpoint from BigQuery SQL, enabling access to the full Vertex AI Model Garden including Claude, Llama, and Mistral models.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training is charged per TB of data processed similar to standard BigQuery query pricing. LLM inference via ML.GENERATE_TEXT is billed through Vertex AI at standard Vertex AI pricing per 1,000 characters or tokens depending on the model. Vector Search queries are charged per query and index storage. BigQuery editions (Standard, Enterprise, Enterprise Plus) on capacity-based pricing include ML features at no additional compute surcharge beyond slot consumption.

databases.name: PostgreSQL
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector similarity search capabilities directly to any PostgreSQL instance, making it the lowest-friction path to vector search as no new infrastructure is required. It supports storing vector embeddings as a native column type, exact and approximate nearest neighbor search using IVFFLAT and HNSW indexing algorithms, and L2 distance, inner product, and cosine similarity operators. pgai (from Timescale) extends pgvector by adding SQL functions to call embedding models and LLMs directly from PostgreSQL, enabling chunking, embedding generation, and LLM inference through SQL queries. pgvector integrates natively with Snowflake Postgres (announced February 2026) and works within existing PostgreSQL security, backup, and replication frameworks. The combination allows building full RAG pipelines entirely within the database.
databases.llm_integration: pgai provides native SQL integration with OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Cohere, and Ollama (for local models) directly from PostgreSQL functions. Embeddings can be auto-generated and kept in sync with source data via pgai vectorizer. Snowflake Postgres with pgvector connects to Cortex AI models. Standard PostgreSQL deployments on AWS RDS, Azure Database, Google Cloud SQL, Supabase, and Neon all support pgvector.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use. Costs depend on the PostgreSQL hosting environment: self-hosted has only infrastructure costs, while managed services like Supabase (free tier available, pro from $25/month), Neon (free tier available, from $19/month), AWS RDS (standard RDS instance pricing), and Timescale Cloud (from $17.63/month) add their own pricing layers. LLM API calls made via pgai are billed by the respective LLM provider at their standard rates.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.ai_feature: Aurora ML + Redshift ML + Amazon Bedrock Integration
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML integrates Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend, allowing SQL-based invocation of ML model endpoints for in-database inference. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector for native vector storage and similarity search. Amazon Redshift ML allows data analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using simple SQL commands, with model training automatically handled by Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. Redshift ML supports classification, regression, and clustering use cases. Both Aurora and Redshift have integrated Amazon Bedrock connectivity, enabling direct invocation of foundation models including Claude (Anthropic), Titan (Amazon), Llama (Meta), Mistral, and Stable Diffusion via SQL or stored procedures without data leaving the AWS ecosystem.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora PostgreSQL integrates with Amazon Bedrock via the aws_bedrock extension, supporting text generation and embedding calls from SQL. Redshift supports Amazon Bedrock model invocation via the ML.PREDICT function and external Lambda functions. Supported Bedrock models include Anthropic Claude 3.5, Amazon Titan Text and Embeddings, Meta Llama 3, Mistral, and Cohere Command. Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector supports full vector similarity search alongside Bedrock embedding generation.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference is charged per Aurora Capacity Unit (ACU) consumed plus SageMaker endpoint pricing for hosted models. Redshift ML training uses SageMaker Autopilot billed per training job; predictions use Redshift compute with additional per-prediction costs for SageMaker-hosted models. Amazon Bedrock is billed on a pay-per-token basis varying by model (e.g., Claude 3.5 Sonnet at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens as of early 2026). pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional licensing cost beyond standard Aurora pricing.

databases.name: Databricks
databases.description: Databricks provides a comprehensive AI and ML platform centered on Mosaic AI (formerly Databricks ML), which encompasses MLflow for experiment tracking and model lifecycle management, the Databricks Marketplace for sharing models and data, Vector Search for embedding storage and retrieval, and AI Playground for LLM experimentation. DBRX is Databricks' own open-source foundation LLM, competitive with GPT-3.5 class models, available for fine-tuning on proprietary data within the Databricks platform. Unity Catalog governs all data and AI assets including models and vector indexes. Databricks Model Serving provides scalable inference endpoints for both open-source and fine-tuned models. The Lakehouse AI architecture allows ML workloads to operate directly on Delta Lake data without ETL, and LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations are native.
databases.llm_integration: Databricks supports integration with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and self-hosted open-source models (Llama 3, Mistral, DBRX, Mixtral) via the AI Gateway (MLflow AI Gateway). Foundation Model APIs provide pay-per-token access to curated models including Meta Llama 3 and DBRX directly within Databricks notebooks and pipelines. Databricks Vector Search stores embeddings in Delta tables and supports automatic embedding sync with source data. RAG chain building is supported natively via Mosaic AI Agent Framework.
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks pricing is based on Databricks Units (DBUs) consumed by compute clusters. MLflow is open-source and free; the managed MLflow on Databricks is included in platform pricing. Vector Search is billed per DBU for indexing and query compute plus storage costs. Foundation Model API pay-per-token pricing applies for hosted model inference (e.g., Llama 3.1 70B at approximately $0.50–$0.99 per million tokens). Model Serving endpoints are billed by DBU per hour of endpoint uptime plus per-token inference costs. Enterprise agreements typically include DBU commitments with volume discounts.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing, indexing, and querying vector embeddings natively within MongoDB Atlas collections alongside operational document data, eliminating the need for a separate vector database. It uses a hierarchical navigable small world (HNSW) algorithm for approximate nearest neighbor search and supports filtering by document metadata fields simultaneously with vector similarity queries (pre-filtering and post-filtering). Atlas Vector Search integrates natively with popular AI frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, and Spring AI. The $vectorSearch aggregation pipeline stage allows combining semantic search with MongoDB's full aggregation pipeline capabilities. Atlas also supports hybrid search combining vector similarity with full-text Atlas Search (BM25) for improved retrieval precision in RAG applications. Quantization support reduces index size and improves query performance for large-scale deployments.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas Vector Search integrates with OpenAI (including text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large), Cohere Embed, Google Vertex AI Embeddings, Amazon Bedrock Titan Embeddings, Hugging Face, Nomic, and Voyage AI for embedding generation. LLM orchestration is supported via LangChain, LlamaIndex, and direct API integrations. MongoDB Atlas has published reference architectures for RAG applications connecting Atlas Vector Search with OpenAI GPT-4, Anthropic Claude, and Google Gemini. No proprietary LLM is embedded natively; MongoDB serves as the vector store layer in the AI stack.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 and above dedicated clusters. Pricing is based on the underlying Atlas cluster tier (M10 starts at approximately $0.08/hour, M30 at approximately $0.54/hour). Vector index storage is charged at Atlas storage rates ($0.25 per GB/month on most cloud providers). There is no separate per-query charge for vector search beyond the cluster compute cost. Atlas Flex (serverless successor) pricing is consumption-based per read/write processing unit. Free tier (M0) does not support Atlas Vector Search.
